questions.source: LC Biology HL 2020, Section C, Question 13 (c)
questions.stem:
The following table shows the representative composition of blood plasma, glomerular filtrate and urine from a typical adult, (each in g/100 cm3 of fluid).

| | Blood Plasma | Glomerular filtrate | Urine |
| Urea | 0.03 | 0.03 | 1.8 |
| Glucose | 0.1 | 0.1 | 0 |
| Proteins | 7 | 0 | 0 |

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Using the data from the table above, what is the main difference between the composition of blood plasma and glomerular filtrate? Explain why this is so.

points.answer: Plasma has proteins (7 g/100 cm3), filtrate has none

points.answer: 1. Glucose (molecules) small enough to pass through (the glomerulus wall) or all the glucose passes through (or is filtered)
2. (All) glucose is reabsorbed (back into the blood)

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Using your knowledge of homeostasis and excretion: 1. State the effect on the volume of urine produced by a high salt intake. 2. Explain your answer to part 1.

points.answer: 2. Makes (walls of) collecting duct (or of distal tubule)

questions.stem: The diagram shows a nephron from a human kidney which plays a part in the filtration of blood.

diagram.what: Coloured drawing of a nephron with its blood vessels (red = arterial, blue = venous, purple capillaries). A dashed red line marks the Cortex (above) / Medulla (below) boundary. Glomerulus in Bowman's capsule at top left; coiled tubule in the cortex (A points to one of its coils, part of the tubule leading from the capsule to the loop); the loop of Henle dips into the medulla with capillaries ('Blood vessels' labelled) around it, B pointing to the bottom of the loop; a second coiled tubule leads to a long branched tube on the right labelled 'Collecting duct containing urine'.

labels.A: proximal convoluted tubule (traced from Bowman's capsule; no official answer)

parts.text: The structure labelled B has evolved to be longer in certain animal species such as camels and desert rats. Suggest an advantage this provides to these animals.

parts.rule: likely: any one or two points

not_covered: Function of the urinary bladder (storing urine until it leaves through the urethra) and how urine moves along the ureter. No question asks about the bladder's role; 2026 Q17(c) only has it drawn and labelled, and 2006 Q6(b) contrasts ureter with urethra.

Where each substance is reabsorbed along the nephron, and how. Glucose and amino acids are taken back by active transport in the proximal convoluted tubule, and the PCT is adapted for this (microvilli, many mitochondria); water and salts are reabsorbed in the loop of Henle and DCT. Questions only touch this in general terms (2004 Q12b(ii), 2008 Q13b(iv), 2024 Q17c(iv)) and never ask for the whole comparison.
The term 'osmoregulation' in humans (control of the body's water and salt balance by the kidney and ADH). It is never asked to be explained; only the 2004 scheme accepts it as an answer.

ADH negative feedback when the blood is too dilute, e.g. after drinking a lot of water: osmoreceptors in the hypothalamus, less ADH, less permeable collecting duct, a large volume of dilute urine. This direction is only accepted as the 'converse' (2022 Q15b(vi)) or implied by the graph in 2025 Q17c(v).
